text: Monday, back underground: E-grade Gate 1107, a storm drain in Mapo. Walking first, stiff as a doll, is Nib, playing husk.
Nib's bare foot sinks a brick under the water. Click.
Darts shoot from the wall. Nib tips his head a hair, and they hiss past his ear without him breaking stride.
Then he turns and tells the client's leader his grip is wrong. He'll lose a finger.
Did his husk just talk? Jaeha, sweating: ventriloquism, sir. It's a hobby.
Picture it: Jaeha the ventriloquist, and a dummy that looks ready to kill.
Nib goes still again, but Bomi's stream caught it. The husk talked. Ventriloquism, the chat howls.
Why is Jaeha here? The rent is overdue. Fifty thousand won base, ten thousand per trap.
And Bomi is filming for BomBom TV: the trap-tester who came back from the dead.
Yerin asks why she agreed to this. Because she quit, Jaeha says, and they both need rent.
New rules in the notebook. One: Nib stays silent. Two: field form only when nobody's watching.
Rule one lasted five minutes, Jaeha whispers. The man was going to lose a finger, Nib whispers back.
Nib's eye slides toward a dark side tunnel. His ear twitches.
The clients jeer. Hurry up, trap rat. They're not paying him to sit in the water.
He isn't sitting. He's marking a hair-thin tripwire. Number six. Ten thousand won each.
Nib walks straight into it like a good husk, and a net crashes down just behind his heels.
Jaeha, deadpan: and that's trap number seven. Very lucky husk.
At a junction where five tunnels meet, violet eyes glint from every dark mouth.
Then the ash rats pour out, dozens of them: hairless, grey, knee-high, all yellow teeth.
The client leader swings wild and misses. The spearman falls on his backside.
Bomi fires with her eyes shut. The arrow hits the ceiling, and a falling brick flattens a rat.
She hit one! Did everyone see that?
That gives Jaeha an idea. Bomi, the big one went down that tunnel! Get it on camera!
The drone zooms off down a tunnel with nothing in it.
Now nobody's watching. A window: Nib, field form, five minutes, linked.
Nib tears through the swarm like a blade, and the rats burst into violet ash.
From above, it's a spiral of ash, the swarm thinning ring by ring.
One rat slips past and clamps onto the spearman's calf.
Yerin drops beside him, hands glowing. Hold still. He's not dying in a sewer.
Down the empty tunnel, Bomi wants to bring the drone back. There's nothing down there!
Go deeper, Jaeha shouts, sweating. Big ones always hide!
Jaeha reads the swarm. The next wave comes from both left tunnels. Cut them off where they meet.
Nib lands right there and slashes both ways, and the rats pile into each other. Nobody sees the drone's red light blink back at the tunnel mouth.
Yerin watches with her hands over her mouth. The clients have their eyes squeezed shut.
Then it's over. Not one rat left. Field form ends after one minute twelve.
The drone returns to drifting ash and one very still husk. Where did all the rats go?
Then the swarm mother squeezes out: twice their size, with bony spurs down its back.
Nib is on cooldown, so Jaeha grabs the leader. When it steps on that brick, the darts fire. Hit it right after.
The darts slam home, and the leader drives his sword into its neck. With the right grip.
Boss defeated: Swarm Mother, E-grade. A new kind of boss is worth ten percent per Operator level, so Route Alignment jumps from thirty to sixty.
They splash for the exit as the tunnel flakes into light, Nib trying hard to look like a husk that can't run.
The leader shows off his new grip. The husk was right. A very observant husk, sir.
Outside at dusk: fifty thousand base, plus seven traps. A hundred and twenty thousand won.
The bitten spearman bows to Yerin. She didn't even flinch. Not this time, she says.
Jaeha looks at the thin fold of notes. The rent is three hundred.
Bomi's stream peaked near five thousand, and the chat has a name for them: the trap rats.
The Trap Rats, Bomi decides. That's their team name now! Jaeha points out that it's an insult.
It's a brand, she winks. Her subscribers just went up by three thousand.
Yerin pushes her share back. Keep it for the rent. He can pay her when they're rich.
Bomi sticks the drone in Nib's face for a comment. Jaeha slides in between. Husks are very shy.
That night, the landlady blocks the stairs. Jaeha bows and offers the hundred and twenty thousand. The rest by Friday.
She snatches the cash and squints at Nib. Friday. And no pets.
Nib stares at her in total, silent offence.
Later, above a closed family restaurant in Mangwon, one window is still lit.
Bomi's room. One hundred thousand subscribers, she tells herself, and Mom and Dad keep the restaurant.
On her desk, a photo of a little girl between her parents on the restaurant's opening day.
She pauses the sewer footage on one blurred frame: a small masked shape, moving far too fast.
She zooms in. A cracked white mask, and beside it, one glowing amber eye.
Bomi's eyes narrow. Husks don't move like that.
